rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's proof turns on refusing love for anything liable to set, not on setting alone; therefore it does not depend on a special contrast with rising.
rows.anchor: إنما هو بعدم تعلق الحب لا بالأفول حتى يوجه العدول إليه من البزوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute concerns whether celestial beings govern the earthly or human realm, not whether they are the ultimate source of all existence and governance.
rows.anchor: نفي ربوبية الأجرام الثلاثة بمعنى تدبيرها للعالم الأرضي أو العالم الإنساني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators make setting proof of contingency, which entails dependence on a necessary existent; Tabatabai says this misses the pagans' actual position.
rows.anchor: قول بعضهم إن الأفول إنما أخذ مبدءا للبرهان لأنه يستلزم الإمكان

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others infer from setting as motion that a mover must ultimately be unmoved; Tabatabai says this proof targets deniers of a creator, not star worshippers.
rows.anchor: ما في قول آخرين إن الأفول إنما ينفي الربوبية عن المتصف به لأنه حركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabians and star worshippers already regard celestial bodies as dependent on God, so contingency and motion arguments do not answer their claim to subordinate governance.
rows.anchor: وعبدة الكواكب من الصابئين وغيرهم وإن ذهبوا إلى أن كل جرم سماوي قديم زماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that setting means contingency or motion misrepresents its proponents: they infer those consequences from setting rather than defining the word that way.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء لا يقولون إن الأفول في الآية بمعنى الإمكان أو بمعنى الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mere disappearance cannot disprove lordship: God is unseen without changing, and celestial disappearance is due to Earth's daily motion and our changed viewpoint.
rows.anchor: الواجب تعالى أيضا غائب عن مشاعرنا من غير أن يتحول عليه الحال

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says setting and rising both indicate origination, but setting is clearer to ordinary people because a star loses its apparent power then.
rows.anchor: وقد أراد الرازي أن يجمع بين الوجوه جميعا فقال في تفسيره ما نصه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi distinguishes audiences: motion's proof of origination is certain but subtle, while setting's visible loss of dominion is evident to everyone.
rows.anchor: أما دلالة الأفول فإنها دلالة ظاهرة يعرفها كل أحد

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: For the spiritually discerning, setting signifies contingency: every possible thing remains dependent until the chain ends at the one beyond possibility.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المحققين الهوي في خطرة الإمكان افول

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: For an intermediate audience, setting signifies motion; every moving thing is originated and depends on the eternal, powerful Creator.
rows.anchor: وأما الأوساط فإنهم يفهمون من الأفول مطلق الحركة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: For ordinary viewers, a setting star loses light, power, and authority, so it cannot be divine; one phrase addresses all three levels of understanding.
rows.anchor: وأما العوام فإنهم يفهمون من الأفول الغروب

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi adds that astrologers considered planets weak near western setting, making setting especially damaging to their claim of celestial divinity.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أصحاب النجوم أن الكوكب إذا كان في الربع الشرقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi's audience-based layers are neither indicated by the verse nor effective against star worshippers, who already treat celestial bodies as dependent beings governing what lies below.
rows.anchor: ما تفنن به من تقسيم البرهان إلى حصص مختلفة باختلاف النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Motion proves that a thing is originated with respect to its moving description, not that its underlying substance began to exist; the full proof belongs elsewhere.
rows.anchor: الحركة إنما تدل على حدوث المتحرك من حيث وصفه وهو التحرك لا من حيث ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham argued from what God showed him in the heavens and from visible phenomena as the conversation allowed, either because he had not seen every daily event or to use evidence his people could observe.
rows.anchor: ساق هذه الحجج بحسب ما كان الله سبحانه يريه ملكوت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omission of the sun may mean the daytime debate with his family and people left no time before night; clouds or the people's presence only at sunrise are other possibilities.
rows.anchor: من المحتمل أن يكون قد خرج إلى قومه للمحاجة والوقت لا يسع أزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people appeal to fear of divine anger and punishment, the stronger motive for worship; hope for blessings has less force because people attribute material fortune to effort, inheritance, or luck.
rows.anchor: الذي بعثهم إلى اتخاذ الآلهة وعبادتها أحد أمرين الخوف من سخطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an correspondingly emphasizes warning more than glad tidings, although both are prophetic methods and duties.
rows.anchor: نرى أن القرآن يذكر الإنذار من وظائف الأنبياء أكثر من ذكر التبشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's people use fear to dissuade him from Allah's lordship and urge him to accept their gods; his reply addresses both rejection of Allah and affirmation of their gods.
rows.anchor: اختار قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام في محاجتهم إياه عندما كلموه في أمر الآلهة سبيل الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plain reading of “my Lord has guided me” is that Abraham has settled knowledge from God's showing him the kingdom of heaven and earth, so further inquiry is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: إني واقع في أمر مفروغ عنه ومهتد بهداية ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More deeply, guidance itself proves God's lordship: guiding someone to the true Lord is an act of governance, and another being would not guide Abraham to reject its own divinity.
rows.anchor: استدلال بنفس الهداية لا استغناء بالهداية عن الاستدلال وتقريره أن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's opponents could claim that one of their gods afflicted him and forced him away from their worship, as the people of Hud accused Hud of divine affliction.
rows.anchor: نظير ما شافهت به عاد هودا عليه السلام لما دعاهم إلى توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the realm in which the people live for sound and well-ordered purposes.
rows.anchor: مملكته التي أوجدها لغايات صحيحة متقنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not leave beneficial or harmful events within His realm unattended: He either prevents them or permits them.
rows.anchor: لا يستقبله بأحد أمرين إما المنع أو الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's encompassing knowledge means no event occurs in His realm without His knowing and either preventing or permitting it; any hypothetical fear would therefore attest His lordship.
rows.anchor: فهو يعلم كل ما يحدث ويجري من خير وشر في مملكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-fear statement completes the guidance argument and also stands as a full proof against the partners; the exception is a concession, knowledge explains it, and the closing question appeals to innate reason.
rows.anchor: فقوله { ولا أخاف ما تشركون به } كالمتمم للحجة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take Abraham's mention of guidance to mean he needs no further argument, though Tabatabai objects that the context presents an argument.
rows.anchor: أورد أكثرهم فيه الوجه الأول من الوجهين اللذين قدمناهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the exception mean God could revive and empower the idols to benefit or harm, so their power would itself show they are created.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه إلا أن يغلب ربي هذه الأصنام التي تخوفونني بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That interpretation wrongly attributes benefit and harm to the partners, contrary to the Qur'anic teaching that only God possesses either.
rows.anchor: تخالف التعليم الإلهي في كتابه فإن القرآن يصرح أن لا يملك نفعا ولا ضررا إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving the idols would not answer pagans, who already accept that idols and their lords are created and dependent on God, even if some are timeless.
rows.anchor: لا يضر أهل الأوثان فإنهم كما عرفت لا ينكرون كون الأصنام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the exception from every kind of fear: Abraham fears any punishment or misfortune God wills, whether as recompense or without prior cause.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن معنى الاستثناء إني لا اخاف شركائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai calls this reading strained because it shifts from fear of the partners to all possible fears without support from the sentence.
rows.anchor: ووجه التعسف في هذا المعنى لا يحتاج إلى بيان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Commentators say the statement about God's knowledge may praise Him, taunt the idols' ignorance, or explain that He knows hidden matters and acts only wisely.
rows.anchor: إنه ثناء منه عليه السلام لربه بعد إتمام الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt would more naturally invoke God's power, while the explanation that He does only what is good should mention wisdom as well as knowledge.
rows.anchor: فما وجه العدول عن القدرة إلى العلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take God's knowledge as explaining the exception: He may already know He will allow harm, such as an idol falling on Abraham or the sun's heat injuring him.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه كالتعليل للاستثناء بجواز أن يكون قد سبق في علمه تعالى إصابته بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge alone is not the most fitting explanation for harm; power or wisdom would better ground that claim.
rows.anchor: التمسك بالقدرة أو الحكمة أنسب للتعليل من العلم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A further interpretation says God's all-encompassing knowledge and will leave no creature able to affect His actions through intercession or other influence; it cites the throne verse.
rows.anchor: علم ربي وسع كل شيء وأحاط به ومشيئته مرتبطة بعلمه المحيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The all-knowledge interpretation does not work by knowledge alone: it also needs unrestricted power and will, which the proposed explanation itself invokes.
rows.anchor: هذا الوجه لا يتم بسعة العلم وحدها وإنما يتم بها وبإطلاق القدرة والمشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited intercession verses affirm causal mediation by God's permission; they do not deny intercession, and the Qur'an consistently recognizes causation.
rows.anchor: الآيات المذكورة مسوقة لإثبات الشفاعة بمعنى التوسط في السببية بإذن من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham exposes a contradiction: they tell him to fear powerless partners while failing to fear Allah, to whom they attribute partners without any revealed proof.
rows.anchor: حالهم يكذب مقالهم ومحصله أنكم تأمرونني أن أخاف ما لا يجب أن يخاف منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone creates and owns, He would have to disclose any divine partnership through revelation or external signs; neither exists.
rows.anchor: فله الملك وله الحكم فلو كان اتخذ بعض مخلوقاته شريكا لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction that God sent no warrant is needed where Abraham points out their own unsupported association, so it also defines the partners he says he does not fear.
rows.anchor: مقيد بحسب ما يستفاد من المقام بما قيد به قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warrant clause does not imply God might authorize partners; it simply says they have no evidence for a superstitious claim of benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: وصف شركائهم بأن الله لم ينزل بها عليهم سلطانا افتراض استدعاه نوع الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument has the form: if God had revealed authority for their partners, fearing them would be justified; He revealed none, so their worship and fear are unjustified.
rows.anchor: لو كان الله نزل بها عليكم سلطانا يدل على قدرتهم على الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in “sent down with it” can indicate accompaniment or causation.
rows.anchor: للمعية أو السببية وقد كنى عليه السلام عنهم وعن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “which of the two groups” avoids provoking pride and emphasizes that the parties are divided over the foundational truth.
rows.anchor: كنى عليه السلام عنهم وعن نفسه بالفريقين ولم يقل أنا وانتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument needs no separate explanation that the qualification is sarcastic or inherent in false partners; the absence of evidence itself resolves the issue.
rows.anchor: فلا حاجة إلى القول بأن التقييد بقوله { لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا } للتهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several linked nominal clauses strongly assert that safety and guidance belong to believers who have not covered their faith with wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: تأكيدا قويا من جهة اسنادات متعددة في جمل اسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Covering is a metaphor: wrongdoing does not erase innate faith, but conceals it and blocks its proper beneficial effect.
rows.anchor: فهو استعارة قصد فيها الإشارة إالى أن هذا الظلم لا يبطل أصل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although wrongdoing is general in form, the context narrows it to the kind that harms faith and suppresses its good effects.
rows.anchor: المراد بالظلم هو نوع الظلم الذي يؤثر أثرا سيئا في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People broadened wrongdoing from unjustly violating social rights to violating laws, committing sins, disobeying God, and even unintentionally damaging their own health.
rows.anchor: توسعوا بعد ذلك فسموا كل مخالفة لقانون أو سنة جارية ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every kind of wrongdoing harms faith: mistakes from forgetfulness, ignorance, or lack of awareness do not obstruct faith's path to true felicity.
rows.anchor: ما كل فرد من أفراده بمؤثر أثرا سيئا في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse conditions faith's protection from the misery of sins on avoiding wrongdoing that corrupts faith's effect.
rows.anchor: اشتراط الإيمان في إعطائه الأمن من كل ذنب ومعصية يفسد أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voluntary wrongdoing varies with understanding: at the threshold of monotheism, shirk is the wrong that blocks faith's safety.
rows.anchor: فالظلم اللائح لهذا الإنسان هو الشرك بالله والإيمان بغيره بالربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After monotheism, major sins such as disobeying parents, consuming an orphan's property, murder, adultery, and drinking wine are the relevant wrongdoing; avoiding major sins brings forgiveness for lesser ones.
rows.anchor: وعده الله أن يكفر عنه السيئات والمعاصي الصغيرة إن اجتنب كبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At higher spiritual levels, wrongdoing includes disfavored acts, neglecting recommended acts, indulging in permissible things, moral failings, and whatever obstructs love and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: كإتيان المكروهات وترك المستحبات والتوغل في المباحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith secures each person only when free of wrongdoing appropriate to that spiritual rank; in this debate the wrong is shirk and the safety is from eternal punishment, while the verse independently has broader force.
rows.anchor: فالإيمان في كل من هذه المراتب إنما يؤمن المتلبس به ويدفع عنه الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith here first means belief in lordship; excluding wrongdoing specifies belief in Allah's true lordship and rejection of partners, distinguishing warranted faith from unsupported partner worship.
rows.anchor: المراد بالإيمان هو الإيمان بالربوبية دون الإيمان بوجود صانع العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's universal application concerns every sin that harms faith, safety from its misery, and release from its misguidance, though its immediate debate concerns shirk.
rows.anchor: وكذا المراد بالأمن مطلق الأمن من شقاء المعاصي والذنوب

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A commentator reads wrongdoing universally to include harm to oneself or others, in religious or worldly life, and takes security to cover both religious punishment and worldly consequences.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين في معنى عموم الظلم في الآية

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The commentator says God may forgive many worldly wrongs through mercy and may punish or forgive in the afterlife for sins short of shirk.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الله تعالى لسعة رحمته لا يعاقب كل ظالم على كل ظلم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The commentator says absolute safety from divine punishment is unavailable to accountable people except for the reverential awe of the spiritually complete.
rows.anchor: أن الأمن المطلق من الخوف من عقاب الله الديني والدنيوي أو الشرعي والقدري جميعا لا يصح لأحد من المكلفين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: If the wrongdoing means major shirk, the commentator says believers are safe from eternal punishment while remaining between fear and hope for lesser sins.
rows.anchor: وأما معنى الآية على فرض عدم الإطلاق فهو أن الذين آمنوا ولم يخلطوا إيمانهم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: He also claims the verse is universal and cites the Companions' understanding as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال وظاهر الآية هو العموم واستدل عليه بفهم الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects the commentator's reading: the Companions understood wrongdoing as sin, whereas his universal definition includes non-sinful acts.
rows.anchor: ما استدل عليه من العموم بفهم الصحابة هو غير ما قرره من معنى العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes faith's effects when not covered by wrongdoing; it does not describe every effect of wrongdoing, such as accidental damage to bodily health.
rows.anchor: وأما ما لا يعد معصية كأكل الغذاء المضر بصحة البدن خطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If no accountable person can meet the commentator's absolute condition, his reading leaves the verse with no real instance and no argumentative benefit.
rows.anchor: ولازمه سقوط الكلام عن الفائدة، وأي فائدة في أن يوضع في الحجة

rows.speaker: الراوندي
rows.claim: A report describes Nimrod's order to separate men and women after a prediction that a child would destroy his rule; Abraham was hidden in a cave and miraculously nourished and grew there.
rows.anchor: فحجب النساء عن الرجال فلم يترك إمرأة إلا جعلت بالمدينة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Through Abu Basir, Imam al-Sadiq reports that Azer, Abraham's uncle and Nimrod's astrologer, foretold the birth of a child who would destroy Nimrod; the narrative then recounts Abraham's hidden birth.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال كان آزر عم إبراهيم منجما لنمرود

rows.speaker: صاحب البحار
rows.claim: Al-Majlisi identifies al-Rawandi's account with the other report and says its wording was changed to fit Imami principles; he treats reports making Azer Abraham's biological father as taqiyya.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن ما رواه الراوندي هو هذا الخبر بعينه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The same story is also attributed to al-Qummi, al-Ayyashi, and Sunni transmitters, including Mujahid, al-Tabari, al-Tha'labi, and early scholars.
rows.anchor: وروي من طرق أهل السنة عن مجاهد، ورواه الطبري في تاريخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith and historical authorities broadly agree that Abraham was hidden in a cave as a child to escape Nimrod, then challenged his father, people, and king over worship and lordship.
rows.anchor: علماء الحديث والآثار كأنهم مجمعون على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام كان في بادي عمره

rows.speaker: أهل التاريخ
rows.claim: Historians call Abraham's father Tarakh and explain Azer as a nickname, an idol's name, or a description; Sunni scholars disagree, while Shi'i scholars generally deny Azer was his biological father.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أن هذا المشرك الذي سماه القرآن أبا إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai says the Qur'an already establishes that the pagan Azer in this passage was not Abraham's biological father; reports saying otherwise conflict with scripture and need not be explained as taqiyya.
rows.anchor: الآيات دالة على أن آزر المشرك الذي يذكره الله تعالى في هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits from Imam al-Sadiq that God unveiled the earth and its inhabitants, the heavens and their inhabitants, the throne and its bearer to Abraham, and did likewise for Muhammad and Ali.
rows.anchor: قال كشط له عن الأرض ومن عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai cites parallel reports from al-Saduq, al-Ayyashi, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Suddi, and a Kafi report identifying the throne-bearers as scholars entrusted with God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي من مفسري السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traditions about unveiling the kingdom interpret other reports on Abraham's vision and support Tabatabai's preceding explanation.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث تفسير سائر الأخبار الواردة في تفسير إراءة الملكوت

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports from Abu Basir that Abraham prayed against three adulterers he saw, then God told him not to pray against servants, whom He created in three classes, including future worshippers born from sinners.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال لما رأى ملكوت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai calls the narration widely transmitted and lists versions in al-Kafi, al-Saduq, al-Ihtijaj, and Sunni collections, including marfu' reports and exegetical mauquf versions.
rows.anchor: أقول والرواية مستفيضة ورواه في الكافي مسندا عن أبي بصير

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
rows.claim: One of the two Imams says Abraham was seeking his Lord when he saw a star and had not reached disbelief; anyone who reflects in that way is like him.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال في إبراهيم إذ رأى كوكبا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports al-Sadiq's view that Abraham did not commit shirk by saying “this is my Lord”; he was seeking his Lord, whereas such a statement by another person is shirk.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي قال وسئل أبو عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai distinguishes Abraham, still seeking before conclusive explanation, from anyone who is no longer a seeker after clear proof has been established.
rows.anchor: الذي هو طالب من تم له البيان وقامت له الحجة الواضحة فهو غير طالب

rows.speaker: حجر
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits Hajar's question to al-Sadiq about Abraham's words; the Imam repeats that Abraham sought his Lord, while the same words from another are shirk.
rows.anchor: عن حجر قال أرسل العلاء بن سيابة يسأل أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: محمد بن حمران
rows.claim: Asked about Abraham's words, al-Sadiq says they did not amount to anything and that Abraham intended something other than the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن محمد بن حمران قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai explains that “this is my Lord” carries no assertion beyond its wording: Abraham used a hypothetical concession or assumed premise to expose its false consequence.
rows.anchor: لا يتعدى مفهوم نفسه وليس له وراء ذلك معنى يحكي عنه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: When the verse troubled people who thought everyone sins, the Prophet explained that the intended wrongdoing was shirk, as Luqman calls it great wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai identifies the “righteous servant” in the report as Luqman and infers that al-An'am was revealed after Luqman; shirk is the contextual application and cannot be forgiven like other sins.
rows.anchor: المراد بالعبد الصالح لقمان على ما حكاه الله تعالى من قوله

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report says a traveler accepted Islam after asking the Prophet about faith, then died in an accident; the Prophet counted him among those with faith and no wrongdoing and said he had earned much reward with little action.
rows.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله قال خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In the same report, the Prophet says he saw the deceased receiving fruit from the houris, and the narrator explains that the man had died hungry.
rows.anchor: هذا من الذين عملوا قليلا وأجروا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai notes similar versions from Ibn Abbas and the Prophet, and a report in which a man asks about the verse before a new Muslim fights and is martyred.
rows.anchor: ورواه أيضا عن الحكيم الترمذي وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس نحوه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali says the verse was revealed specifically about Abraham and his companions, not this Muslim community.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects restricting the verse to Abraham's community because faith and wrongdoing affect innate human nature across all peoples and eras.
rows.anchor: الآية لا تشتمل بمضمونها على حكم خاص تختص به أمة دون أمة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A commentator speculates that Abraham's community needed only monotheism because Hammurabi's code supplied civil and ethical law, while Muslims were accountable to a complete revealed law.
rows.anchor: لعل مراده أن الله خص إبراهيم وقومه بأمن موحدهم من عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects the Hammurabi explanation: its chronology does not fit Abraham's era, and the king's own inscriptions invoke numerous pagan gods.
rows.anchor: حمورابي هذا كان يعيش على رأس سنة ألف وسبع مائة قبل المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Abraham's people had no revealed law beyond monotheism is contradicted by Qur'anic reports of prayer, good works, almsgiving, pilgrimage, lawful livestock, separation from polytheists, moral prohibitions, purification, and greeting.
rows.anchor: يكذبه أن القرآن يحكي عن لسان إبراهيم عليه السلام الصلاة كما في أدعيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the religion “the faith of your father Abraham” shows that its roots include principles and branches, though it does not prove every detailed later ruling existed in Abraham's time.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن لم يدل على أن هذا الدين على ما فيه من تفاصيل الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier revelation taught prophets and communities universal principles for worship, social life, and morality, directing them toward good and away from injustice and corruption in every kind of society.
rows.anchor: الوحي الإلهي كان يعلم الأنبياء السالفين وأممهم أصولا كلية في المعاش والمعاد
